action.text: Task: Add regression tests for port access on urlsplit/urlparse results. Implementation (parse.py:177-185): port property checks isdigit()+isascii(), raises ValueError('Port could not be cast to integer value as {port!r}') for non-digit/non-ASCII, then checks 0<=port<=65535, raises ValueError('Port out of range 0-65535'). Error occurs at .port access, not construction. Empty port ('' after colon) is stored as None by _hostinfo (not port → port=None), so .port returns None, NOT an error. Cases: None→None, ''→None (same as no port), 0→0, 65535→65535, 65536→range error, -1→cast error, abc→cast error, \u0966→cast error (not ASCII). Bytes: same logic. Candidate: 918f0684. Test sha: d25ffa0e. Fix: move empty port to valid assertions (assertIsNone), remove from invalid lists. Then doc file.

action.new:
# No port at all → None
            p = parse("http://example.com/")
            self.assertIsNone(p.port)
            p = parse(b"http://example.com/")
            self.assertIsNone(p.port)
            # Empty port (colon with nothing after) → None
            p = parse("http://example.com:/%")
            self.assertNotEqual(p.netloc, "example.com:/%")
            p = parse("http://example.com:/%")
            self.assertIsNone(p.port)
            p = parse(b"http://example.com:/%")
            self.assertIsNone(p.port)
            p = parse(b"http://example.com:/%")
            self.assertIsNone(p.port)
            # Port 0 (lower bound)
            p = parse("http://example.com:0/")
            self.assertEqual(p.port, 0)
            p = parse(b"http://example.com:0/")
            self.assertEqual(p.port, 0)
            # Port 65535 (upper bound)
            p = parse("http://example.com:65535/")
            self.assertEqual(p.port, 65535)
            p = parse(b"http://example.com:65535/")
            self.assertEqual(p.port, 65535)

        # Invalid ports: ValueError raised at .port access, not at parse.
        # Each entry is (port_value, expected_message).
        str_invalid = [
            # One above upper bound
            ("65536", "Port out of range 0-65535"),
            # Negative: minus sign makes it not a digit string
            ("-1", "Port could not be cast to integer value as '-1'"),
            # Non-integer: letters
            ("abc", "Port could not be cast to integer value as 'abc'"),
            # Non-ASCII decimal digit (Devanagari 6)
            ("\u0966", None),
        ]
        bytes_invalid = [
            (b"65536", "Port out of range 0-65535"),
            (b"-1", "Port could not be cast to integer value as b'-1'"),
            (b"abc", "Port could not be cast to integer value as b'abc'"),
        ]
